title: Commercial cleaning: build the first U.S. operation around accounts and routes
description: Test the customer contract, staffing, supervision and cash collection before assuming a local manager can run the model.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Define the account cluster before the territory
paragraphs: Compare customer types, usable service hours, site access, journey times, frequency and contract length. A contract that works well in the home market demonstrates delivery there; it does not establish U.S. labour availability, customer demand or procurement acceptance.
Identify the supervisor’s practical area and what happens when accounts have conflicting service windows. A large geographic territory is not a substitute for a workable route.

sections.heading: A manager does not remove the other management jobs
paragraphs: Assign who estimates labour, wins bids, covers absences, responds to complaints and collects invoices. Price dedicated management and quality supervision before assuming a royalty is affordable. If the overseas founder still performs those jobs, that dependence needs to be visible.

Test customer concentration separately. Losing one large building can remove revenue while supervisory time, vehicles and route gaps remain. A broad sales forecast may hide that account-specific problem.

sections.heading: Separate workplace duties from customer purchasing conditions
paragraphs: OSHA, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, identifies cleaning-industry chemical, equipment and workplace hazards and links applicable general-industry standards. The responsible employer needs an actual task/product safety review. This page does not establish safety clearance for a particular job.

A customer may also require insurance evidence, background screening or a particular service level. Record those as customer purchasing conditions unless independently required by law. Identify their source and cost rather than treating every requested document as a government licence.

sections.heading: Fictional example: investigate three nearby office buildings
paragraphs: A fictional brand investigates three nearby buildings instead of assuming a national rollout. For each, it records the bid process, service times, access, equipment storage, staffing cover, customer sign-off and collection terms. Missing travel or wage information remains missing, rather than improving the market score.

The team asks whether one supervisor can support the actual schedule and who replaces an absent worker. Finance follows invoice acceptance, disputes and expected receipts alongside payroll. The exercise produces questions and evidence requirements, not invented margins or a successful pilot result.

sections.heading: Use the customer’s payment terms in the cash plan
paragraphs: Contracted revenue, an accepted invoice and money received are different events. SBA’s finance guidance is a useful accounting reference; the operator needs its own dated costs and collections to see the funding requirement. A profitable annual estimate does not show whether the next payroll can be met.

For national accounts, record who receives the work, which operator serves each site and who invoices. A paid pilot must be arranged lawfully; evidence from delivery does not itself authorise offers of franchise rights.

sections.heading: Prepare the next bid as a repeatable management process
paragraphs: Create an account-level brief that operations and finance can both use. Keep the customer’s renewal and termination provisions with the service and cash assumptions.
bullets: Record the customer, tender date and actual contract conditions.
Map service hours, travel, supervision and cover.
Separate legal duties from customer and insurer conditions.
Track invoice approval, disputes and actual cash dates.
Define national-account allocation and lawful pilot responsibilities.

practicalOutput: An account-level pilot brief showing the route, staffing, customer conditions, management duties and invoice-to-cash timing.
limitations: No location-specific wage, tax, customer demand or safety clearance.
learningSummary: For an established cleaning company, the useful operating unit may be a cluster of customer accounts rather than a shop. A U.S. partner needs enough nearby work, appropriate staff and management, and money to pay costs before customers pay. This guide explains how to investigate that practical model without treating home-market success as proof of U.S. demand.

keyTerms.meaning: How closely accounts and service times fit together, affecting travel, staffing and supervision.
The customer’s process for selecting a supplier and agreeing the work.
Amounts invoiced to customers but not yet collected.
Dependence on a small number of customers, so losing one can materially affect the operation.

title: Facilities services: split the customer bundle into actual jobs
description: One contract can contain several trades, subcontractors and cash responsibilities.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Describe each activity inside the facilities promise
paragraphs: List cleaning, planned maintenance, access systems, pest control, landscaping, repairs and any other work actually included. Record what the partner performs, subcontracts or only coordinates. A facilities brand licence does not itself authorise every task.

State the worksite and contracting/employing business. Professional, contractor and sector requirements can affect which business may deliver a particular service and what it must retain or supervise.

sections.heading: The customer contract needs named operating responsibilities
paragraphs: A service-level agreement can cover response time, completion evidence, exclusions, escalation and credits. Decide who dispatches, approves extra work, invoices, responds to emergencies and bears rework costs. A single sales promise may need several teams behind it.

Customers may require specific insurance, references or approved subcontractors. Keep those purchasing conditions distinct from government and insurer requirements so the operator understands their actual source and price.

sections.heading: Investigate permissions by activity and location
paragraphs: SBA, the U.S. Small Business Administration, directs businesses to licensing requirements according to their activities and locations. Begin with the actual state, municipality, county and site rather than assuming a universal facilities-services licence.

A subcontractor’s own licence does not automatically resolve all obligations of the main contracting or employing business. Identify the authority and actual question for each job. This article provides a planning method, not a permission for the whole bundle.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a multi-site customer pays on 60-day terms
paragraphs: A fictional partner wins a multi-site customer with 60-day invoice terms. It must pay technicians and subcontractors earlier, while the customer can dispute work if completion evidence is missing. The financial question therefore includes both gross margin and dated cash collection.

The team follows a job from dispatch to customer sign-off, invoice and payment, recording who fixes missing evidence. It also tests the effect of that national customer failing or withholding payment separately from a broad market-sales percentage. The 60 days are fictional contract terms, not a statutory deadline or an actual customer result.

sections.heading: Price the coordination, not just the technician’s visit
paragraphs: Include emergency cover, subcontractor selection and management, reporting, rework and any agreed credits. If a job crosses an operator’s territory, specify who may accept it, deliver it and invoice it. An informal understanding can leave both support and cash costs unclear.

SBA’s finance guidance supports the distinction between accounting and cash questions; the actual contract and receipts determine the model’s inputs. Do not claim a complete funding answer from a quoted margin alone.

sections.heading: Build a service-by-service table before the full offer is promised
paragraphs: For each task show the worksite, contracting business, employer, delivery lead, subcontractor if any, relevant public authority and customer conditions. Add response, evidence and payment responsibilities. This suggested table makes the one-contact promise understandable to the people who must deliver it.
bullets: Separate performed, subcontracted and coordinated services.
Identify the actual permission question and responsible party.
Record customer and insurer conditions separately from law.
Price emergency response, rework and coordination.
Connect national-account allocation to invoice and cash timing.

practicalOutput: A service-by-service table showing delivery, permissions, customer conditions, performance responsibilities and payment timing.
learningSummary: A facilities brand may promise a customer one point of contact for cleaning, repairs, landscaping and other services. That is convenient commercially, but each underlying activity still needs the right operator and any applicable permission. The brand and local partner should define both who delivers the work and who pays for it while waiting for the customer.

keyTerms.meaning: The contract’s performance requirements, such as response, completion evidence, exclusions and credits.
A separate business engaged to deliver part of the customer service; its role does not automatically settle the main contractor’s duties.
A contractual adjustment associated with the agreed service terms, to be read from the actual contract.
The customer’s process for accepting the invoiced work, which can affect when money is received.

title: Pest control: connect the product, applicator and operating jurisdiction
description: A U.S. product source and an experienced overseas team do not settle every local permission.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the treatment rather than the territory map
paragraphs: List the target pest, treatment method, site, product and people applying or supervising it. Separate the product’s lawful status, the individual’s certification and any business licence. Home-country training may demonstrate experience, but does not itself establish U.S. authority.
The same service description can need different answers in different places or categories. Identify those questions before assigning the technician or assuming the brand manual is sufficient.

sections.heading: Understand the federal starting point and local administration
paragraphs: EPA, the Environmental Protection Agency, explains certification for restricted-use pesticide applicators or supervisors under the relevant rules. State, territorial and tribal authorities administer certification. Many states have broader requirements for commercial work.

Check each actual operating jurisdiction and category. Do not assume certification automatically travels across a state boundary. This page does not decide a particular state certificate, supervision arrangement or product authorisation.

sections.heading: Importing and applying are different responsibilities
paragraphs: If the brand proposes importing a familiar treatment, identify the actual product, importer and applicable product/establishment and arrival requirements. EPA’s import guidance does not turn a foreign approval into permission for ordinary U.S. use. The applicable exceptions and shipment route require their actual conditions.

Using a U.S.-sourced product may change stock logistics but does not erase applicator or business requirements. Keep product, person, business and jurisdiction records connected without treating one as proof of the others.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two neighbouring states are not one permission
paragraphs: A fictional European brand proposes importing a treatment and starting in two neighbouring states. The team divides the investigation into lawful product/import supply and each state’s people/business requirements. For each proposed job, it records the relevant site, product use, person and supervision question.

It then compares a U.S. supply option against the actual service specification. The exercise grants no import permission or certification. It shows why a convenient bottle source and a nearby state border do not settle the operating plan.

sections.heading: Make route economics reflect the actual service
paragraphs: Recurring accounts can improve route density, but callbacks, emergencies, seasonal demand, product storage and access conditions affect capacity. A very wide territory can consume supervisory travel time. Record actual customer insurance requests and spill, vehicle and product-use responsibilities rather than treating an insurance quote as approval.
Price the qualified supervision and backup needed for the first market before assuming a royalty is affordable. Unsupported certificate, fee, coverage or demand inputs should remain unresolved.
bullets: Record products and label-directed sites/uses.
Name the certifying authority and category for each area.
Identify qualified people and required supervision.
Assign storage, transport, notice and incident questions.
Collect evidence for seasonality, travel and callbacks.

practicalOutput: A product/person/business/jurisdiction table linked to route capacity, supervision and the unresolved launch requirements.
limitations: No state certification or specific product conclusion.
learningSummary: A pest-control brand can provide a method and recurring customer contracts, but the U.S. operator needs appropriately authorised people and products for the actual work. Federal certification is a starting point, with state, territorial and tribal administration and potentially broader commercial requirements. Build those facts into route and staffing plans before promising coverage.

keyTerms.meaning: The product category for which the cited EPA guidance explains applicator/supervisor certification requirements.
The relevant qualification for applying or supervising the covered pesticide work, distinct from product status.
An operating permission for the business where required, separate from an individual’s certification.
A return service visit, which affects the capacity and cost of the recurring route.

title: Industrial maintenance: prove the delivery behind a response promise
description: Customer qualification, hazardous-energy duties and specialist cover belong in the first-market plan.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Define the equipment and work before the brand promise
paragraphs: Industrial maintenance can include inspection, machine servicing, electrical tasks and process-critical repair. State the equipment and boundaries of the job, who can approve an exception and when specialists must be called. A broad maintenance description does not establish permission for every activity.
Customer engineering approval, site access and procurement can also determine whether the partner can deliver. Record those conditions separately from public professional or trade requirements.

sections.heading: Hazardous-energy duties need actual task assessment
paragraphs: OSHA, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, explains hazardous-energy risks in servicing/maintenance and points to 29 CFR 1910.147. For covered work, the responsible employer needs appropriate energy-control procedures and training.

Identify the real task and host/contractor interface. This overview does not decide exemptions or replace the customer-site procedure. Construction, maritime, State Plan and particular trade questions need their own applicable analysis; a brand checklist is not an actual safe-work determination.

sections.heading: Translate response time into people, travel and resources
paragraphs: A four-hour response promise is a staffing, geography and spare-parts decision. Identify on-call pay, specialist cover, travel, calibration, tools, insurance and subcontractors before pricing it. Do not assume the same technician can meet every overlapping call.

A customer’s production-loss exposure is different from the service fee. Liability terms and service credits belong in the actual contract and financial review. No universal allocation or insurance adequacy is established here.

sections.heading: Fictional example: investigate one industrial corridor
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch brand chooses one corridor for customer interviews and a lawfully arranged pilot. It asks what a supplier must demonstrate before bidding, how shutdown work is scheduled and who approves a new technician. The team describes the actual equipment and potential demand rather than using a national population total as evidence.

It then tests the proposed response promise against dispatch, specialist availability, travel and parts. Missing information remains a question to resolve, not an assumed successful pilot or financial result. The exercise does not authorise a task or replace site procedures.

sections.heading: Compare recurring contracts with shutdown projects
paragraphs: Recurring maintenance income and one-off shutdown jobs can create different capacity and cash requirements. Record their staffing, customer approval and collection conditions separately. SBA’s finance material is a reference for the accounting/cash distinction, not a source of actual U.S. margins.
The support organisation must also be funded without assuming repeated territory-sale fees. A large territory grant cannot make a sparse customer base or missing specialist capacity disappear.

sections.heading: Prepare the first-corridor brief
paragraphs: Show assets and tasks, competent people, customer purchasing/safety/insurance conditions and the relevant local trade questions. Give technical escalation and backup clear owners.
bullets: Define what the partner performs and when work is referred.
Identify the actual customer qualification process.
Build the required task-specific safety and training arrangements.
Test response time with supported travel, staff and parts assumptions.
Separate recurring, project and continuing-support costs.

practicalOutput: A first-corridor brief showing exact tasks, qualified delivery, customer conditions and the resources needed for the response promise.
limitations: Task-specific OSHA, state-plan and trade scope remains to be reviewed.
learningSummary: An industrial-maintenance brand may be judged on how quickly it can restore a customer’s operation. The U.S. partner therefore needs to establish the precise work, qualified people and customer access conditions before selling broad coverage. This guide connects those practical decisions with the limited hazardous-energy starting point and the costs of specialist response.

keyTerms.meaning: The customer’s process for deciding which suppliers and people it will accept for the work.
The energy risks in servicing and maintenance addressed by the cited OSHA overview and applicable standard.
The people and arrangements available to respond outside ordinary scheduled work.
A contractually defined consequence of the agreed service terms, to be checked in the actual contract.

title: Technical services: find the decisions that still depend on the founder
description: Test whether another manager can use the method, recognise its limits and obtain qualified help.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: List the exceptions the founder handles
paragraphs: Record unusual jobs, specifications, supplier substitutions, pricing decisions and warranty disputes. For each, note frequency, required response time and the consequence of a wrong or late decision.

A general independence score cannot show whether those decisions have transferred. The useful evidence is what a proposed manager can actually do using the documentation, and where the method still requires another qualified person.

sections.heading: Experience and legal authority are separate questions
paragraphs: Divide tasks into inspection, advice, design, installation, repair or certification. Requirements depend on the actual activity, state, profession and site. SBA’s licensing-by-activity/location approach is a starting point, not a professional credential decision.

A foreign qualification or brand licence does not settle U.S. authority. Equally, customer accreditation or acceptance requirements should not be mistaken for government permission. Record the actual source and conditions of each requirement.

sections.heading: Price the technical decision channel
paragraphs: Include quotation help, complex faults, documentation, audits and customer meetings in the support budget. If a U.S. manager must wait overnight for the European founder, a customer response promise can fail even when the field staff are capable.

Name the primary and backup decision makers and distinguish the brand, partner and appropriately authorised professional roles. Cost remote support and necessary visits instead of treating the founder’s continuing effort as free.

sections.heading: Fictional example: work through ten past exception jobs
paragraphs: A fictional German testing-services brand selects ten historic exception jobs with sanitised information. A proposed manager records the decision they would make, what information is missing and when they would escalate. The responsible technical lead compares the reasoning with the method and its limits.

The team uses disagreements to identify unclear documentation or missing support. It then tests the revised process on the defined exercise. This does not confer professional competence, predict future outcomes or approve actual testing work. No confidential customer details need to be inserted into the learning exercise.

sections.heading: Keep the business choice narrower than the ambition
paragraphs: A bounded U.S. pilot can investigate whether the manager, support channel and customer requirements fit together before broad rights are granted. State what the pilot is intended to test and which actual permissions must already be established.

SBA finance guidance is a useful reference when separating operating costs and cash questions. It does not provide the missing wage, travel or support quote. Keep those inputs tied to the real proposed organisation.

sections.heading: Prepare a decision-and-support table
paragraphs: Give every founder-only decision a proposed local owner, permitted limits, evidence and backup. Record which decisions must remain with the brand or an appropriately authorised person rather than insisting that every task becomes local.
bullets: Map technical, pricing and customer exceptions.
Name qualified primary and backup decision makers.
Retain training and observed-performance evidence.
Separate customer acceptance from government authorisation.
Cost support and define the actual pilot before wider grants.

practicalOutput: A decision-and-support table showing local authority, limits, evidence, escalation and backup for work previously owned by the founder.
limitations: No professional credential or regulatory approval is issued.
learningSummary: A technical company can have branch managers while its founder still decides every unusual quotation, fault or warranty dispute. That dependence can become expensive when a U.S. partner works in a different time zone. Before granting broad rights, identify the decisions, authorisations and support resources needed to deliver without constant owner intervention.

keyTerms.meaning: Referring a question to a person with the required authority or expertise.
Observed work, training and stated limits supporting a person’s ability, rather than an automatic professional licence.
A customer’s acceptance requirements, distinct from government authority.
A suggested table naming who may decide what, when to refer it and who provides backup.

title: IT services: decide who gets access and who responds when something goes wrong
description: Connect the customer, partner and overseas support team before promising continuous service.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Draw the actual service and access relationships
paragraphs: IT support, software implementation, managed services and training need different access. Record who contracts with the customer, whose staff access systems, where access occurs, what data is involved and who authorises changes.

Brand software rights, the customer’s own licence and permission to access a system are different things. A partner’s right to use the brand does not answer what customer information its technicians may see or change.

sections.heading: Use cybersecurity guidance for the role it actually plays
paragraphs: NIST offers small-business guidance on cybersecurity risks, incident response, cloud security and related topics. Use it as a preparation reference. It is not a universal law, a service endorsement or certification of the proposed business.

Actual customer contracts, public contracts, sector requirements and privacy law need their own evidence and applicability assessment. Keep a recommended internal control distinct from a specific legal obligation.

sections.heading: Make the support hours affordable and deliverable
paragraphs: A U.S. customer may need service while the parent team sleeps. Price on-call cover, specialist escalation, third-party licences, secure onboarding/offboarding, backups, incident exercises and reporting. A 24/7 promise needs the people and supplier commitments behind it.

Decide who may approve emergency work, who funds it and who may communicate externally about an incident. Record applicable contractual and legal deadlines without inventing one reporting period for all customers and incidents.

sections.heading: Fictional example: rehearse before granting live customer access
paragraphs: A fictional Southeast Asian managed-service brand gives one U.S. partner a limited support role. In a test environment, the teams rehearse removing a departed technician’s access and responding to a suspicious-login report.

They record who receives the report, who can make the relevant changes, how the overseas team is reached and what happens if it is unavailable. The result is evidence of an exercise, not proof of legal compliance, a secure real system or absence of risk. No actual customer data is required for this learning task.

sections.heading: Turn the rehearsal into a usable operating document
paragraphs: Prepare an access-and-incident responsibility schedule showing customer, brand and partner entities, actual data paths, named approvers and the access needed for each role. Limiting access to the work needed is a practical design recommendation here, not a universal legal determination.

Keep cross-border privacy and sector restrictions unresolved until assessed. Supplier licences, security services and customer-specific cover need actual cost assumptions. SBA finance guidance can support the accounting approach but does not supply those quotes.

sections.heading: Prepare for either business being unavailable
paragraphs: Test how support continues if the parent or partner cannot respond. The goal is to understand the dependency before a customer relies on the promise.
bullets: Record actual systems, data, locations and staff access.
Name access approvers and removal responsibilities.
Assign incident, customer and supplier communications.
Record actual applicable deadlines rather than one universal period.
Budget and test backup cover for the promised service window.

practicalOutput: An access-and-incident schedule linking systems, people, approvals, communication and backup cover to the actual customer promise.
limitations: No comprehensive federal/state or cross-border privacy assessment.
learningSummary: An IT-services brand may deliver through a U.S. partner while specialist support stays overseas. Customers need to know who may access their systems, approve changes and act on an incident. The operating plan should connect those responsibilities with the staffing and supplier commitments behind the service promise.

keyTerms.meaning: Ongoing support or operation of agreed customer systems, whose actual duties must be described in the contract.
The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which provides the small-business cybersecurity guidance cited here.
An event needing the relevant security response; the actual legal and contractual reporting duties must be determined separately.
Removing or changing access when a worker or business relationship ends.

title: Business training: explain what the learner’s certificate actually means
description: Separate course rights and teaching capability from occupational or education permission.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Describe the learning service and the promised outcome
paragraphs: Distinguish corporate workshops, technical instruction, assessment and a course marketed as qualifying someone for an occupation. State what the learner receives and who recognises it. An attendance certificate, private brand credential, occupational licence and recognised qualification are different records.

This matters to both sales audiences. The prospective partner needs to understand what it may deliver and promise; the learner or corporate customer needs an accurate description of the course and credential.

sections.heading: Investigate the actual activity and location
paragraphs: SBA’s general licensing guidance connects requirements with business activity and operating location. Record where teaching, student recruitment, assessment and customer contracting occur. Licensing a syllabus does not itself establish authority for all those activities.

If the offer touches a regulated occupation, childcare, healthcare or postsecondary education, investigate the relevant requirements before making sales promises. This article does not determine a professional or education exemption or approval.

sections.heading: Give the partner usable content and instructor rights
paragraphs: Record who owns and may use the slides, software, recordings, marks, learner materials and translations. Identify who updates technical content and who approves instructors. A curriculum can become unusable if the agreement does not provide the actual delivery rights.

A successful home-market branch may also depend on the founder’s teaching or reputation. Observe whether another instructor can deliver the defined outcome using the materials and stated assessment criteria, rather than assuming a training manual replaces that capability.

sections.heading: Fictional example: follow one paid corporate workshop
paragraphs: A fictional European business-to-business training brand tests one paid corporate workshop through a properly reviewed arrangement. It records customer procurement, instructor preparation, venue/platform cost, travel, materials, cancellation terms and the expected collection date.

The teaching observation and customer requirements help identify preparation and delivery work that a classroom-revenue calculation would miss. No fictional profit or successful learning result is assumed. Multiplying a full classroom’s gross revenue by every working day is not evidence of likely profit.

sections.heading: Connect course economics with realistic delivery
paragraphs: Price preparation, customer acquisition and realistic utilisation alongside classroom time. Record which cancellations or customer approval conditions affect cash and what resources the brand must continue to supply. SBA’s finance guidance is a reference for the accounting and cash distinction, not a source of actual demand.

Keep outcome claims tied to actual evidence and the credential’s true status. If the course is changed or marketed for a different purpose, revisit the relevant rights and permission questions rather than reusing an old workshop description.

sections.heading: Prepare the course-and-delivery factsheet
paragraphs: Create a document showing the course, actual audience, promised credential, materials/translation rights, instructor approval, revision responsibility and remaining legal questions. That makes the product understandable to the partner and to the people who will teach it.
bullets: Describe attendance and qualification claims precisely.
Identify sector and education questions before promotion.
Record actual material rights and update ownership.
Observe another instructor against defined criteria.
Price preparation, utilisation and acquisition rather than only classroom sales.

practicalOutput: A course-and-delivery factsheet explaining the credential, content rights, instructor evidence, realistic costs and unresolved permission questions.
limitations: No professional or education authorisation determination.
learningSummary: A training brand may offer corporate workshops, technical instruction or courses advertised as a route into an occupation. Those services do not all raise the same questions. The expanding business should define what learners receive, what rights a partner can use and what another instructor can actually deliver before selling a standard programme.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidence of attendance; it is different from a licence to practise or a recognised professional qualification.
A credential issued under the brand’s own system, whose meaning must be stated accurately.
The rights governing use of the materials, software, recordings, marks and translations.
How much of the realistically available teaching capacity is actually used for paid work.

title: Can your team run the business when the owner is absent?
description: Test who makes important decisions before assuming branch managers make the model ready to transfer.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Daily delivery can hide exceptional decisions
paragraphs: Ask about sales, prices, major customers, technical exceptions, supplier negotiations, recruitment, quality problems and cash approvals. A manager may organise routine delivery while the owner handles the unusual matters that determine whether a contract is won or a customer retained.

The title branch manager is therefore useful information, but not the conclusion. The question is what happens when the owner cannot answer the telephone. This is a commercial preparation exercise; there is no statutory management-readiness score in this guide.

sections.heading: Map responsibility and actual authority
paragraphs: For each important responsibility, record the accountable role, day-to-day decision maker, backup and authority limit. Add the most recent observed example and any restriction. A written manual is not the same evidence as a manager successfully using it under realistic conditions.

Include both recurring work and consequential exceptions. If only the owner can approve a customer concession, identify that dependency rather than marking customer management fully delegated. A gap is a useful investigation result, not a reason to award an optimistic transferability score.

sections.heading: Worked example: the COO delivers, the owner sells
paragraphs: Fictional example. A facilities company’s chief operating officer, or COO, reliably runs service delivery. The owner still closes every contract above a company-chosen internal limit. The team initially budgets a U.S. delivery manager and assumes the business can run without the owner.

The responsibility map exposes the missing sales job. The U.S. plan needs someone with actual sales authority, enough time for customer purchasing processes and a defined level of parent support. Finance costs the people who would replace that work separately from routine management. The SBA finance guidance supports disciplined cost and cash planning; it does not prescribe a required manager salary.

sections.heading: Test a bounded, reversible absence
paragraphs: Choose an internal exercise such as a planned week with documented escalation arrangements. Select ordinary tasks and exceptions in advance, identify who may decide and keep essential customer protections in place. Record who acted, delays, rework and customer effects.

If a manager repeatedly waits for owner approval, ask what authority, knowledge or commercial relationship is missing. If the team performs well, record the scope and conditions of that success. One internal exercise is not proof of U.S. delivery capability or legal compliance.

sections.heading: Use the result to change the plan
paragraphs: The next decision might be more documentation, training, a different hire, a smaller pilot or a pause. Re-test after a meaningful change in the service offer, team or customer mix. Keep parent support costs visible instead of describing the overseas owner’s time as free.

The concrete output is a responsibility map showing authority, backup, observed examples, costs and unresolved dependencies. Use it before selecting a partner structure or promising support that the current organisation cannot yet provide.

practicalOutput: A responsibility map showing owner-dependent decisions, tested cover, replacement costs and dated evidence.
limitations: Business preparation only; no statutory readiness threshold.
learningSummary: An established business can have capable managers and still rely on its owner for the decisions that win customers or protect profit. That matters when a partner will operate in the United States while the owner stays overseas. Investigate the actual work the owner performs before deciding what a local manager and parent support team must replace.

keyTerms.meaning: The ability of the team to make and carry out the important decisions when the owner is absent.
The boundary of what a person may approve without referring the decision elsewhere.
The person who can actually take over a task with the necessary knowledge and authority.
Sending a question to a person with the authority or expertise to resolve it.
A dated example of someone performing the responsibility, rather than a statement that they should be able to.

title: Area developer or master operator: who will do the extra work?
description: Compare contracting, payments, recruitment and ongoing support before setting U.S. network rights.
reviewStatus: Merged into canonical guide after near-duplicate editorial review

sections.heading: Decide functions before labels
paragraphs: An own-unit operator delivers services in its own business. An area developer undertakes to open its own units over time. A master arrangement can authorise the recruitment and support of subfranchisees. An area representative may assist recruitment or support while the brand remains the contracting franchisor. Distribution and IP licensing need their own goods, payments and control facts.

sections.heading: Map three kinds of flow
paragraphs: Draw contracts, money and operating support separately. Who grants rights to the unit operator? Who collects initial and continuing payments? Who provides initial training, approves operators, supports bids, monitors quality and handles disputes? The definition in 16 CFR 436.1(k) includes subfranchisors performing pre-sale and post-sale functions; allocation in a contract does not erase regulatory duties.

sections.heading: Compare capability and funding
paragraphs: A partner may run excellent branches while lacking the staff and systems to recruit independent owners. List the extra roles and cost them before offering broad rights. Model the recurring support office using the revenue it can actually retain after the brand split, tax assumptions and obligations; treat unknown withholding as unresolved.

sections.heading: Fictional decision
paragraphs: A fictional brand expects the first partner to operate two branches, then recruit others. Phase 1 own-unit evidence should not automatically satisfy Phase 2 recruitment and support readiness. Write a separate decision gate with ownership, funding, sales-law review and support-capability evidence.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: a responsibility and payment diagram.
bullets: Identify every contracting and fee-receiving entity.
Separate own units from independent operator recruitment.
Assign pre-sale records and post-sale support.
Budget field visits, training, systems and local compliance work.
Test a delayed network and no new upfront fees.
Record unresolved federal and state definitions, disclosure and exemption questions.

limitations: No label-based franchise classification or allocation of legal liability.

title: What evidence supports your first U.S. business-customer market?
description: Compare how customers buy, how the team will deliver and what the first useful test can establish.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Define the service and customer before ranking cities
paragraphs: State which customer type you want, the exact service, likely contract, purchasing requirements and practical service radius. A facilities buyer, a factory and a small office can have different needs even in the same city.

A commercial region is useful for comparing markets, but it is not a legal authority. The actual city, county, state and address can still change the operating requirements. Do not treat a large metro or your home-market reputation as evidence of local acceptance.

sections.heading: Keep three types of evidence separate
paragraphs: An interview records a stated need. A tender invitation records an opportunity to compete. A signed customer contract creates obligations under its actual terms. None automatically establishes the next stage: interest is not an award, and an award is not proof of profitable delivery or timely payment.

For each observation, record the source, date, limit and next question. Ask what evidence would change the decision. That produces a more useful record than counting every positive conversation as a likely sale.

sections.heading: Choose the comparison criteria before seeing the result
paragraphs: Possible criteria include customer fit, sales-cycle length, staffing, route density, access to support, operating requirements and payment terms. Let the team choose the importance of each factor, then identify the evidence supporting its assessment.

Keep critical unknowns visible. Missing insurance or permit cost must not become an attractive zero. If a decisive factor lacks evidence, withhold the overall ranking rather than create a precise-looking score from incomplete inputs. This is recommended planning practice, not a legal market-selection formula.

sections.heading: Worked example: an office cluster or a wider territory
paragraphs: Fictional example. A pest-control brand compares a compact office cluster with a larger but dispersed territory. The wider area offers more apparent prospects, while the cluster might permit shorter journeys and a smaller initial team.

The brand interviews actual buyers, checks the relevant service categories and obtains local staffing and insurance evidence. It tests whether customer needs and purchasing conditions fit its offer. The compact area may be easier to investigate, but that remains a hypothesis until supported. A small pilot also needs the appropriate legal review before offers, hiring or operations.

sections.heading: Give the next test a document and a decision
paragraphs: Prepare a shortlist showing the customer segment, operating boundary, evidence, costs and important unknowns for each candidate market. Distinguish observed demand from home-market assumptions. Quote costs with their source, date, unit and scope.

Choose the smallest useful next activity, with a responsible person, budget and review date: for example, answering a customer’s actual procurement question rather than granting a statewide territory. The output should explain what was learned and what remains to be tested, without invented search-demand figures or a universal best-market claim.

practicalOutput: A sourced market shortlist and a specific next test, with important unknowns left visible.
limitations: No ranking, search-demand statistics or unsourced cost averages.
learningSummary: A large city population does not prove demand for your particular service. A business-to-business company needs evidence about the organisations that buy it, their purchasing process and the cost of serving them. Start with a narrow customer and operating area before promising a large territory.

keyTerms.meaning: Business to business: selling to organisations rather than assuming the customer is an individual consumer.
The customer’s process for selecting suppliers, approving purchases and awarding contracts.
An opportunity to submit a bid; it is different from a contract award.
How closely customer jobs are grouped, affecting travel and the capacity to serve them.
A planned test designed to answer a specific business question rather than simply collect encouraging comments.

title: Why a service contract can use cash before it produces cash
description: Map the invoice, customer approval and receipt dates alongside payroll and supplier payments.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Ask when the money arrives, not only when the work is earned
paragraphs: In an accrual-based model, service revenue can be recorded before payment is received. Payroll, materials and subcontractors may fall due first. The SBA finance guidance distinguishes cash and accrual accounting; the practical result is that an operating-profit model cannot replace a cash schedule.

Read the customer contract. When may an invoice be submitted, what supporting material is needed, who accepts it, when does the payment clock start and what disputes can delay it? A nominal 30-day term may run from acceptance rather than the technician’s visit. Do not use one assumed collection ratio for every customer.

sections.heading: Worked example: invoices are not receipts
paragraphs: Fictional example. The first month produces $80,000 of invoices but no customer receipts yet. Payroll and other payments due that month total $65,000. On those stated flows, the month uses $65,000 of cash before considering opening cash, financing or other items.

The $15,000 difference between invoices and payments is not automatically accounting profit: the two figures do not establish all revenue and matched costs. More importantly for the launch, an invoice cannot pay wages before the customer pays. Finance adds actual deposits, tax payments, equipment, financing receipts and later collections on their dates to find whether capital covers the low point.

sections.heading: Avoid counting the same money twice
paragraphs: List known payroll and supplier payments once in the dated schedule. If the team also holds a contingency for uncertainty, explain what additional risk it covers. Do not add the same $65,000 again under a generic reserve while also treating it as an operating outflow.

Keep refundable deposits, expenditure and cash retained for later needs distinguishable. A financing promise is not an available receipt until its conditions are supported. The same applies to supplier credit: use the terms actually offered, not hoped-for terms.

sections.heading: Test different causes of delay separately
paragraphs: State downside, base and upside assumptions explicitly. Change the customer start date, collection delay, disputes and staffing commitments as separate inputs so the team can see why the cash position changes.

A large national account may improve delivery density while concentrating cash exposure in one approval process. If that customer pays later, fixed staffing payments may still be due. This is a fictional planning exercise, not a forecast of any customer’s collection behaviour.

sections.heading: Walk the cash balance forward
paragraphs: Start with the supported cash available. Add each expected receipt and subtract each payment when it is expected to occur, then identify the lowest balance. That cumulative low point explains the funding gap more usefully than the single largest monthly expense.

Retain service, invoice, acceptance and receipt dates, the supporting contract or quote and the person updating the assumption. Unknown taxes and uncommitted financing remain unresolved. The output is a dated cash-flow and funding schedule with a named finance owner, not a guarantee that the launch is financed.

practicalOutput: A dated receipt-and-payment schedule showing the cumulative low point, funding gap and assumptions to verify.
limitations: Illustrative amounts are fictional; no customer collection forecast.
learningSummary: A contract can look attractive in an operating-profit budget while the business lacks money on the dates bills fall due. Customers may pay after service, invoicing and approval, while payroll and suppliers need payment earlier. Build a dated cash schedule as well as a profit model.

keyTerms.meaning: Recording revenue and costs under the relevant accounting rules rather than simply when cash moves.
An amount owed by a customer, which is not yet cash in the bank.
The customer’s approval step under the actual contract, which may affect when invoicing or payment timing starts.
Funding used to bridge the timing of operating receipts and payments.
The largest cash shortfall shown as the dated payments and receipts accumulate, before the funding available to cover it.

title: Who owns the national account when local partners deliver?
description: Allocate selling, contracting, service, payment and credit before promising territorial rights.
reviewStatus: Merged into canonical guide after near-duplicate editorial review

sections.heading: A customer can buy nationally and receive service locally
paragraphs: A facilities or technical-services customer may negotiate centrally while operations occur in several partner territories. Separate lead ownership, contracting authority, service obligation, invoice recipient and margin allocation. “Exclusive territory” alone does not answer those questions.

sections.heading: Write an account-allocation schedule
paragraphs: Define reserved existing accounts, newly won national accounts, local branches of national buyers, online enquiries and jobs straddling boundaries. Include response, referral and dispute processes. The schedule should explain who approves pricing and how local delivery costs are considered. In a franchise, territory disclosures and terms need to align; the FTC guide’s Item 12 discussion is a reference point.

sections.heading: Fictional overlap
paragraphs: A fictional Dutch maintenance partner wins a customer whose headquarters is inside its area but whose first job is elsewhere. Another partner has local capacity. Compare a referral fee, local-service payment and central contract arrangement as commercial options; none is assumed lawful or enforceable without relevant review.

sections.heading: Protect service continuity and investment
paragraphs: Budget sales effort, equipment and training fairly. Define what happens if one operator cannot meet a national service obligation or an account changes scope. Avoid promising protection from independent competitors or suggesting that a contractual reservation overrides non-waivable local relationship rules.

sections.heading: Preparation checklist
paragraphs: Output: an account-allocation matrix before territory negotiation.
bullets: Classify accounts by actual contracting and service location.
Separate customer acquisition, fulfilment and collection.
Record channel, referral and pricing responsibilities.
Document expense and revenue allocation with an example.
Identify dispute, cure and continuity questions for review.
Make the disclosure and agreement consistent with the intended process.

limitations: No competition-law or territory-term enforceability opinion.

title: How to check whether a prospective U.S. partner can deliver
description: Turn a candidate’s claims about money, management and experience into specific checks before granting U.S. rights.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the work and commitment you are considering
paragraphs: Imagine that your established facilities business wants a U.S. partner to recruit a local supervisor, find customers and fund the first months of operation. Checking whether the candidate has run any business is too broad. You need to know whether it can perform those particular tasks, within the proposed timetable, while meeting its other commitments.

Write down the candidate’s legal business name and identifiers, who would sign, and the authority that person claims to have. Then list the decisions you need to make: whether to grant rights, how large the territory should be, who will run it and how much funding is actually committed. These are recommended business checks, not a government approval process.

sections.heading: Separate wealth, available funding and operating capacity
paragraphs: A statement that someone is wealthy does not establish that money is accessible to the proposed operation. Total assets may include property, money belonging to another company or funds subject to conditions. Record separately the claimed net worth, readily available money, conditions on access and amount allocated to this project.

Management capacity needs its own evidence. A successful owner may be unable to provide the promised supervisor, or that supervisor may already be responsible for several businesses. Ask for comparable delivery experience and references that can explain the work actually performed. Record who checked each claim, when, what they saw and any contradictory information. A blank answer remains an unanswered question.

sections.heading: Keep sensitive documents out of this educational site
paragraphs: This site is for describing checks and recording responsibilities. Do not upload passports, personal court files, bank statements or confidential customer contracts here. A useful entry can say that an authorised adviser holds a dated funding confirmation, identify its limits and name the person responsible for following up, without reproducing the private document.

If a sensitive check is justified, arrange an appropriately authorised professional and secure process outside the tool. Record consent and permitted access where applicable. Collecting more private information does not itself make a decision better: the question is whether the evidence answers a relevant business uncertainty.

sections.heading: Understand what a court search can and cannot show
paragraphs: PACER is the U.S. federal courts’ electronic records service. Its Case Locator is a national index covering federal district, appellate and bankruptcy cases. That does not make it an index of every possible dispute. State and local courts, administrative proceedings, arbitration and foreign records require separate decisions about what to search.

Record the systems, business names and other relevant names searched, the search date and the case outcome or procedural position. An empty result does not prove that there are no disputes. Equally, a complaint contains allegations; finding one does not establish that the alleged misconduct occurred. Read the relevant documents before describing the significance of a result.

sections.heading: Fictional example: impressive assets, unanswered project questions
paragraphs: A fictional British facilities candidate says it has ample wealth and a senior manager ready to lead the U.S. operation. The brand has not established how much money is allocated to this project or whether that manager can leave existing responsibilities. Strong references for the candidate’s older business do not answer either question.

The brand therefore assigns three separate checks: dated confirmation of project funding, references for comparable service delivery, and clarification of the named manager’s competing commitments. It leaves each unverified claim labelled as such. Depending on the answers, it can investigate further, reduce the proposed territory, test a limited pilot or pause the transaction.

sections.heading: Leave with a usable evidence register
paragraphs: Create one row for each important claim, with the decision it affects, evidence requested, custodian, checker, date, limits and next action. This is a practical planning method rather than a prescribed legal form. It helps the team see which commitments the evidence supports and which questions remain open.
bullets: Confirm the entity, relevant identifiers and signing authority.
Distinguish overall wealth from accessible, project-allocated funding.
Check actual operating experience and availability of named managers.
Record reference scope, contradictory evidence and court-search limits.
Assign an owner and deadline to each unanswered question before deciding whether to commit.

practicalOutput: A partner evidence register showing each material claim, its checker and custodian, the date and limits of the check, and the next decision.
limitations: No character, solvency, funding or compliance certification.
learningSummary: An interested partner may have an impressive business and still lack the people or money needed for your U.S. project. Before giving it a territory or signing a long agreement, separate what it has claimed from what someone has actually checked. The result is a record that supports your business decision, rather than a certificate that the person is trustworthy or financially secure.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking information relevant to a proposed business commitment before deciding whether to proceed.
The power of a particular person to enter an agreement on behalf of the business.
Money or assets readily available to meet payments; this differs from total wealth.
The person or organisation responsible for keeping a document or other evidence.
The recorded outcome or procedural position of a court case, such as dismissal or a judgment.

title: How to compare franchise disclosures for a business run by a hired manager
description: Read costs, support, owner duties and financial evidence together before treating another franchise’s results as a model for yours.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the document before copying a figure
paragraphs: Start with the seller’s legal entity, brand, issue date, amendment dates and applicable state addenda. Keep the source link and identify the transaction or territory being discussed. Two documents carrying the same brand name may describe different years or terms. A fee from one version and financial results from another do not form a reliable comparison.

This also matters when you study an established U.S. franchise as a possible comparison for your own foreign brand. A domestic business whose owner sells, supervises and handles exceptions may have a very different cost structure from a new operation employing a manager to do those tasks.

sections.heading: Read the owner’s duties together with the promised support
paragraphs: Item 15 addresses participation in the actual operation of the franchise. Item 11 describes assistance and training, and Item 12 deals with territory. Read these subjects together with the proposed agreement. A sales statement that the business can be manager-run needs support in the actual offering and contractual duties; training alone does not answer who must be present or perform the work.

The FTC’s May 2008 Compliance Guide explains these disclosure subjects. It is explanatory guidance, not an endorsement of an offering or a current threshold sheet. The selected items below organise a comparison, but a reviewer still needs to check all 23 FDD items and the transaction documents.

sections.heading: Build a comparison with a place for unanswered questions
paragraphs: Use separate columns for the document’s wording, its item and page, the model it describes, and the question it leaves unresolved. Do not silently substitute an industry assumption for a missing answer. If software extracts a number or clause, check it against the actual document before relying on it.
bullets: Items 5–8: initial and ongoing fees, other costs, and purchasing or supply restrictions.
Items 11–12: assistance, training and territorial rights or limits.
Item 15: participation in operating the business.
Item 17: renewal, termination, transfer and dispute terms.
Item 19: any financial performance representation and the conditions attached to it.
Item 20: outlet information, the group of outlets being compared and contacts.
Item 21: the seller’s financial statements, which answer a different question from an individual outlet’s results.

sections.heading: Fictional example: established-unit revenue is not a new-unit profit forecast
paragraphs: A fictional service franchise reports revenue for established outlets. Your team plans to open a new territory and hire a dedicated manager. The reported revenue describes sales for a defined group; it does not tell you what will remain after your operation pays its manager and other costs.

First identify the included outlets’ ages, service mix and owner involvement, together with exclusions from the figures. If owners in that group personally supervise staff or win accounts, ask how your proposed model will replace that work. Record costs absent from a revenue figure instead of assuming that they are negligible.

You may conclude that the information is useful for understanding a particular mature business but insufficient for estimating your start-up’s profit. Keep that conclusion and its limits in the worksheet. Do not turn the figure into a profit estimate or a statement to prospective partners without the appropriate supporting basis.

sections.heading: Keep a versioned record the team can revisit
paragraphs: For each offering, retain the document reference, issue and amendment dates, relevant addenda, and exact item or page supporting an entry. Record management duties and the definition of any reported outlet group beside the numbers. Keep the seller’s financial statements separate from outlet performance.

Finish by assigning each unresolved document or interpretation question to a responsible person before commitment. The comparison is a workspace for evidence and decisions. A completed spreadsheet, especially one populated automatically, does not establish that the documents have been fully reviewed or that the proposed model is permitted.

practicalOutput: A versioned FDD comparison linking costs, support, participation duties and financial evidence to the actual document and proposed management model.
limitations: No FDD document extraction is published or deemed verified automatically.
learningSummary: A Franchise Disclosure Document, or FDD, gives a prospective franchise buyer information about a particular seller and offering. It can help your team compare operating models, but it does not approve the business or promise a profit. If your proposed U.S. business will use a hired manager while its owner stays abroad, the central question is whether the documents and performance evidence actually describe that arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: A document disclosing information about a franchise seller and offering to a prospective buyer; its numbered items cover different subjects.
Additional or modified terms supplied for a particular state; these need to be read with the main document.
A statement about actual or potential financial performance, addressed in FDD Item 19.
The defined group of outlets included in a set of reported results.
A business in which the owner does operating work that may need a paid replacement in a manager-run model.

title: How a federal service contract can change a labour-cost bid
description: Check the contract’s coverage, wage determination and staffing duties before reusing the price of a private-customer service job.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: First establish what kind of contract you are pricing
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Labor’s Service Contract Act guidance concerns covered federal and District of Columbia service contracts performed through service employees, subject to exceptions. For covered contracts over $2,500, the applicable wage determination and fringe benefits matter. Coverage cannot be settled from the word “cleaning” or “maintenance” alone.

Identify the buyer, contract type, place of performance and work to be done. A private customer’s request for bids is not automatically a federal service contract. Equally, where you will work as a subcontractor, do not assume that the relevant contract obligations disappear because another business has the direct agreement with the government. The actual coverage, worker duties and exceptions need to be assessed.

sections.heading: Obtain the documents that turn a service description into a cost
paragraphs: Ask for the actual solicitation and its incorporated clauses, the relevant wage determination, job descriptions and work locations. Obtain any relevant facts about the predecessor contract and collective bargaining agreement. These are inputs to the coverage and cost review, rather than interchangeable background documents.

Map what workers will actually do to the relevant classifications in the contract materials. A general title such as “team member” may hide different duties. Use the applicable wage and benefit terms in the model; a generic national minimum wage or the brand’s existing rate overseas does not establish the cost of this particular covered work.

sections.heading: Distinguish legal obligations from the buyer’s other conditions
paragraphs: A buyer or prime contractor may also ask for insurance, registrations, financial capacity, references, security controls or reporting. Record where each requirement comes from: a sourced legal rule, an incorporated contract term or another procurement condition. That makes it easier to identify the responsible person and the evidence needed.

The distinction does not mean that a contractual condition can be ignored. It means the team should avoid describing every item in a bid pack as a generally applicable law. Put the document and clause next to each cost or task, and record any uncertainty that could change the promised service or price.

sections.heading: Fictional example: one supervisor, several cleaning sites
paragraphs: A fictional cleaning partner starts with its private-office bid template. It assumes one supervisor can cover several sites and budgets ordinary cleaner wages. The proposed government work has specific staffing periods, labour categories and reporting requirements. Without the applicable determination and actual duties, the old template cannot establish a reliable bid.

The bid lead obtains the contract materials, and the payroll lead maps jobs and benefits. The operations lead checks whether the supervisor can travel between sites while meeting the required coverage, and whether travel and reporting time have been included in the cost model. These are practical checks on the planned delivery arrangement; this example supplies no wage figure or staffing permission.

The finance lead then places wages, benefits and other start-up payments on the dates money will be needed, alongside the expected customer-payment dates. A price that eventually covers costs may still require cash before invoices are paid. If a material wage, benefit or staffing input remains unknown, record the bid as incomplete rather than treating the missing cost as zero.

sections.heading: Produce a checklist that remains useful during delivery
paragraphs: Keep a solicitation-to-cost checklist owned jointly by the bid and payroll leads. Link each material labour assumption to the relevant document, job and work location. Coverage and applicable terms matter during performance as well as before the bid commitment.
bullets: Record the buyer, contract type, place of performance and proposed worker duties.
Identify the applicable coverage, exceptions and incorporated clauses.
Obtain the relevant wage determination and predecessor-contract facts.
Price the applicable wages, benefits, staffing periods and reporting work.
Test the dates of start-up payments against expected receipts.
Resolve critical unknowns before committing to a price.

practicalOutput: A solicitation-to-cost checklist connecting coverage, clauses, job duties, wages, benefits and payment timing to named bid and payroll responsibilities.
limitations: No specific solicitation, wage determination or exemption decision.
learningSummary: A cleaning or maintenance business may find that a federal service job costs more to deliver than a similar private-office contract. Covered government service contracts can carry particular wage and benefit obligations, so the customer’s required work and contract documents must come before the price. This guide explains what the bid and payroll teams need to obtain; it does not decide coverage or supply a wage rate for a particular job.

keyTerms.meaning: The federal service-contract law addressed by the Department of Labor guidance cited here; its coverage and exceptions need checking for the actual contract.
The buyer’s request inviting bids or proposals, including its work requirements and incorporated contract terms.
The applicable schedule or determination of required wages and fringe-benefit terms for covered work.
Compensation benefits in addition to the basic wage that must be considered under the applicable terms.
The business contracting directly with the buyer, which may engage other businesses as subcontractors.
An agreement with employee representatives that may be relevant when reviewing predecessor-contract wage and benefit facts.
